Your parents' lost shares are not gone. Check this first. India has eighty nine thousand crore rupees of shares, unclaimed.
An old share certificate in a cupboard. A dividend nobody cashed. After seven years unclaimed, the company moves those shares to a government fund, called IEPF.
By November 2025, IEPF held shares worth about eighty nine thousand crore, from sixteen hundred companies. Reliance alone, about fifteen percent of it.
This money belongs to real families. Maybe yours. And dividends earned on those shares can be claimed too. So how do you check?
Step one. Open iepf dot gov dot in. Search your parent's or grandparent's name, under unclaimed amounts.
Step two. Dig out old certificates, dividend letters, and bank passbooks. Ask relatives too. Many families never knew a grandparent owned shares.
Step three. File form IEPF five online, with PAN, ID proof, and bank details. Legal heirs can claim too.
It's slow, but it works. In two years, over seventy five thousand claims were approved, and about four crore shares went back to families.
